What broke: the ingestion pipeline on Thursday Nov 12. A deploy of ingest v2.14.0 (PR ingest#412) raised the default `max_batch_bytes` from 1 MB to 10 MB; with the 512 Mi memory limit, the ingest-worker pods hit out-of-memory on the first large batch and crash-looped, so events piled up in Kafka and dashboards went stale from 08:47 to 12:27 UTC (3h40) [1][3][9]. The deploy went to all pods at once, and we had no consumer-lag alert, so the first signal was a Sentry OOM alert 27 minutes later [1].

No customer data was lost. Events kept arriving in Kafka and were processed late; a reconciliation on Nov 13 confirmed per-workspace event counts matched Kafka offsets for 08:00–13:00 UTC [1][3]. The incident report to customers stated the same: "received and processed late; none were lost" [2].

What we're changing, per the postmortem and incident report:
- KES-431: page on-call when consumer lag exceeds 5 minutes (due Nov 20) [1][10].
- KES-432: ingest config changes go to a small canary pool first (due Nov 27) [1].
- KES-433: raise the worker memory limit to 1 Gi and add a load test on batch sizes (due Nov 27) [1].
- The immediate fix, ingest#419, already reverted the default back to 1 MB and added a guard that refuses batches larger than 25% of container memory [6].
